question: In round 2, after going back to the median-split tree, you tried shrinking the traversal stack to 16 entries with a depth cap of 15. Besides its best time, what render_ms_avg did that 5-frame benchmark print?
answer: That 5-frame benchmark (stack 16 / depth cap 15, median-split tree, 512x512 at 64 spp, seed 1) printed render_ms_avg=126.379 ms, alongside render_ms_best=119.866 ms and gpu_ms_best=119.359 ms, with samples=16777216 (= 512*512*64) and threads_used=8. I know this because the raw run output is preserved in my archived history as message #125; my note in #126 ("Stack 16/depth cap 15 REGRESSED (119.9 vs 103.3ms)") was the reaction to it, and I reverted to stack 20 / cap 16, which measured render_ms_best=103.290 / render_ms_avg=113.313 in #121 and reproduced at 101.77 in #130. Note this early stack-shrink regression is separate from the later one at #304 (stack 20->16 on the near-first kernel: 76.4 vs 62.9 ms best) — both were reverted for the same reason. Current live round-2 state is render_ms_best=59.114 / gpu_ms_best=58.839 at best, ~60-66 ms on repeats.
